title: Adaptive Kernel Selector + Prefill/Decode Scheduler (arch & seqlen aware)
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: We need an adaptive kernel selection subsystem that picks the optimal kernel implementation at runtime based on model architecture, GPU family, and observed sequence-length distribution. Current static heuristics produce 15-40% suboptimal latency on mid/long seq workloads; the goal is an online-autotuner + lightweight decision function that drives kernel choice for prefill and decode phases separately and persists a compact policy per (model, hw_profile).
context: Background: Serving runtime supports multiple kernel implementations (flash_attn variants, tiled attention, fused MHA, quantized kernels). Kernel performance is highly sensitive to: compute capability (A100/H100/L4), tensor core availability, precision (fp16/int8), sequence length distribution, and whether we are in prefill (large batched KV writes) or decode (single-token loop with KV cache accesses). Existing kernel-picker is table-driven with coarse buckets and does not adapt to workload drift or new hardware. This causes tail latency regressions in customer workloads and prevents safe rollout of newer kernels.
proposed_solution: 1) Build a compact kernel registry keyed by (model_arch_family, gpu_family, precision, seqlen_bucket, batch_size_bucket). 2) Add an offline microbenchmark harness to populate baseline latency/throughput/cost for candidates across hardware we support. 3) Implement an online lightweight autotuner: on cold start run short probe micro-benchmarks for hot models; during traffic, collect latency/seqlen histograms and run an optimizer every N minutes to update the chosen kernel. 4) Separate decision paths for prefill vs decode: prefill optimizer prefers throughput/batched kernels and KV-write-friendly memory layouts; decode optimizer prioritizes single-token latency and KV-cache friendly kernels. 5) Persist policy in config store with versioning and rollout flags; expose a metrics endpoint and dashboard for chosen kernel and delta vs baseline.
acceptance_criteria:
- Kernel selector chooses different kernels for prefill vs decode for at least 80% of models where we saw previously poor performance.
- End-to-end p50/p95 latency improves by >=10% on targeted workloads (internal benchmark).
- No increase in error rates or model output divergence beyond existing noise thresholds.
- Autotuner has safety: if new kernel causes >20% p95 regression in 10 minutes, automatically roll back to previous policy.
- Console exposes per-model kernel choice and estimated cost delta; logs for any autotune decision stored for 30 days.

implementation_notes:
- Registry format must be serializable to JSON and small enough to ship with runtime agents.
- Offline harness will run in CI on hardware lab instances: a100-80gb, h100-80gb, l4-28gb. Use representative micro-benchmarks: prefill (seq=1024/512 batch=8), decode (seq=1 batch=1 repeated 512 steps).
- Decision function will be two-layer: fast rule-based buckets first, then table-lookup updated by autotuner. Avoid heavy ML models in-path.
- Prefer deterministic selection for same (model, hw, seqlen_bucket) to make metrics comparable.
- Store telemetry in existing metrics pipeline (prometheus/gateway) with labels kernel_impl, phase, model_hash, hw_profile.
experiments_and_results:
Preliminary lab runs (Mar 09):
- A100, seq=512 batch=4: best new tiled-kernel reduced p50 by 18% and p95 by 12% vs current default.
- H100, seq=32 decode: flash_attn_v3_fp16 gave 22% p95 improvement.
- L4, int8, seq=1024 prefill: quantized tiled kernel improved throughput but increased memory by 8%; acceptable with autoshrink cache.
Notes: microbenchmarks show heavy cross-over points: some kernels win at seqlen<=64, others at >=256. This validates seqlen-aware selection.
rollout_plan:
- Stage 1: internal canary on dev-dedicated pool with no customer traffic.
- Stage 2: 10% traffic on dedicated for non-critical tenants with metrics gated.
- Stage 3: 50% traffic with automated rollback if p95 regresses.
- Stage 4: full rollout.
Each stage requires updated runbooks and an ops rollback button in Console.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Autotuner picks brittle kernels causing regressions under production tail patterns. Mitigation: conservative safety thresholds, require 30 min of sustained improvement before promoting policy.
- Risk: Additional probes increase resource consumption. Mitigation: probes run at very low qps and prefer off-peak windows; reuse warm VM allocations.
- Risk: Policy churn across upgrades. Mitigation: bind policy to runtime version and provide migration tool.
testing_and_validation:
- Unit tests for registry serialization and decision function.
- Integration test suite that runs microbench scenarios in lab (A100/H100/L4).
- E2E smoke tests on canary pool verifying throughputs and model outputs unchanged within tolerance.
- Load test to ensure probe runner does not affect production latency.
